agree.reason: The pay guarantee, the honest note on hours and the open door on schedules will keep many staff listening, but a long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets little reason to want the job beyond keeping a paycheck.

honest.reason: It mostly sticks to the brief's facts and drops the overclaim that everyone's job gets better, but it adds a few things the brief doesn't support: that members already know these staff, the meeting timeline, and a promise to hear schedule needs before shifts are set.

works_the_facts.reason: It does the useful math of turning the severance formula into 20 weeks for a 10-year employee and sets the 44% drop beside the 60% rise, but it doesn't work out anything else, such as what the extra 3 open hours a day mean or how much on-hold time the staff could cut.

right_comparison.reason: It compares shrinking branch work with growing phone work and states the severance option fairly, though it doesn't spell out what happens to these branches or jobs if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: The only conditions are the 90-day wait for work-from-home and a decision deadline left as a placeholder, so the reader can't yet check the dates or the consequences.

objections.reason: It takes on the hours and childcare worry directly, but it ignores the two weeks of rumours ("hear this from me first" will sound hollow to these readers) and only touches the main objection, that they don't want phone work, through the 'members know you' line.

fit.reason: It is a COO's email with a clear subject line and sections, at roughly 470 words, a bit over the 400 asked for.
